topics.topic: Raw SpooledFile byte-read capability: whether it is an exposed action and what authorization/disclosure rules govern it
questions: Are agents allowed to read raw spooled file bytes when disclosure class is not `personal_data`, or are raw spool bytes owner-only regardless of class?
Is reading spooled file bytes a distinct product action in scope now, and who is allowed to perform it?
Is reading spooled file bytes a separate product action (thus part of the fixed surface), or must it be served through existing inspect/read-trace actions, or not exposed at all?

quotes:
The kernel exposes one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect,
author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate,
grant, revoke, resolve and cancel.

Read by the next node that receives
it, by the owner's approval preview and the owner's inspection read of its bytes
(A10 rule 2; the State 5 operation `read_spooled_file`), and by capture into
a trial corpus while its run holds its spool (A15 rule 5).
judgement.why: One passage makes the MCP surface an exhaustive fixed list that does not include `read_spooled_file`, while another names `read_spooled_file` as an operation.

topics.topic: Draft-write resend authority after not_applied: require fresh owner approval or use activation authority only
questions: When a `draft-write` effect is `not_applied` and must be sent again, must the kernel obtain a fresh owner approval (despite `draft-write` normally not stopping for approval), or resend under flow activation authority only?

If a `draft-write` attempt is resolved `not_applied`, must the resend now require an explicit owner approval (creating `owner_approval` waiting), or does `draft-write` remain approval-free even on resend?

quotes:
- `authority`: the approval or the grant it used, or for a `draft-write` send
  the flow activation under which the run started (State 2, A10 rule 6; State
  5) — except a resend after `not_applied`, which, whatever its class, records
  the fresh approval it needed;

Sending again after `not_applied` is a new attempt
under a fresh approval, never under a standing approval (K-08).
judgement.why: The model text explicitly states that a resend after `not_applied` needs a fresh approval regardless of effect class, which covers `draft-write`.

topics.topic: AdmissionVerdict lifecycle on repeated identical submissions (new verdict/trials vs reuse existing)
questions: If the same implementation is submitted again with unchanged corpus, does the kernel create a new AdmissionVerdict (and new TrialExecutions), or reuse the existing verdict record?

topics.topic: Flow activation idempotency: whether re-activating an already active version creates a new FlowActivation record
questions: If the requested flow version is already the active one, must the kernel write a new FlowActivation record or return the current active version without creating a record?

topics.topic: Handling client-supplied disclosure_class on function/flow output ports (reject vs accept-and-ignore)
questions: If an author/composer supplies `disclosure_class` on a function output port or flow output port in a request, must the kernel refuse the request or accept and ignore that field?

topics.topic: ManifestOperation facts for base_url when no service instance is selected
questions: When `service_instances` has no selected instance for a service, what is the `ManifestOperation` fact set for `base_url`?

topics.topic: Run status precedence when a run is simultaneously waiting in one branch and runnable in another
questions: When a run has at least one waiting node and also still has runnable work in other branches, which single status is stored on the Run record at that moment?

topics.topic: Terminal Run records: whether waiting points must be cleared on final statuses
questions: When a run reaches a final status (especially `cancelled` or `refused` while waits existed), must `waiting` be cleared, or may waiting points remain on the final Run record?
